target.title: Word pair classification during imagined speech using direct brain recordings

read.pdf: Figs. 1–5 captions read from text.txt; no tables present; figure images not supplied
read.code: https://github.com/cjlin1/libsvm (upstream library; README, svm-train.c, svm-predict.c checked; no study-specific scripts); https://www.ee.columbia.edu/~dpwe/resources/matlab/dtw/ (Ref. 46 third-party DTW code page, inaccessible)

entries.text: The authors introduce an SVM classification framework using nonlinear temporal realignment in the kernel to handle timing variability in overt and imagined speech.
entries.condition: Pairwise word classification from high-gamma ECoG time courses; DTW supplies the realigned distances.

entries.text: The Methods state that DTW-distance SVM kernels had previously shown superiority over HMMs for speech recognition; this is cited background, not a comparison performed in this study.
entries.condition: Prior speech-recognition work; no HMM baseline was tested in this ECoG experiment.

entries.text: The authors claim the first demonstration of single-trial neural decoding of words during imagined speech production.
entries.condition: Binary decisions between word pairs, not unrestricted vocabulary decoding.
entries.quote: Our results provide the first demonstration of single-trial neural decoding of words during imagined speech production.

entries.text: The authors say imagined-word neural representation is evident in temporal, frontal, and sensorimotor cortex, with the most robust decoding effects in temporal electrodes.
entries.condition: Anatomical interpretation of the ECoG word-pair classification results.

entries.text: ECoG data came from five patients undergoing epilepsy neurosurgery.
entries.condition: Subdural electrode arrays; grid placement and monitoring duration were determined by clinical needs.
entries.loc: Results > High gamma features; Materials and Methods > Subjects and data acquisition

entries.text: The task used six English words: spoon, cowboy, battlefield, swimming, python, and telephone.
entries.condition: The selected words varied in acoustic features, syllable count, and semantic category while minimizing word-length variance.
entries.quote: The choice of stimuli was carefully chosen to maximize variability in terms of acoustic features, number of syllables and semantic categories, but minimize word length variability

entries.text: The six-word vocabulary yields 15 binary word pairs, the full pairwise set evaluated in the study.
entries.condition: Each decision is two-class classification among the six prompted words.
entries.quote: average classification accuracy across fifteen word-pairs was significant across five subjects

entries.text: Each word was repeated randomly between 18 and 24 times.
entries.unit: repetitions per word (task statement; per-subject allocation not further detailed)
entries.condition: Six-word auditory-cued task; trials were presented in random order.
entries.quote: Trials were repeated randomly between 18 and 24 times.

entries.text: Signals were acquired bedside with seven 16-channel g.USBamp devices at 9,600 Hz.
entries.condition: Subdural ECoG acquisition in the epilepsy-monitoring setting.
entries.loc: Materials and Methods > Subjects and data acquisition

entries.text: ECoG was downsampled to 1,000 Hz, DC-corrected, band-pass filtered at 0.5–200 Hz, notch-filtered at 60/120/180 Hz, visually screened, and common-average re-referenced.
entries.condition: Acquisition preprocessing before high-gamma extraction.
entries.loc: Materials and Methods > Subjects and data acquisition

entries.text: Classifier features were high-gamma envelopes extracted with a non-causal order-20 Hamming-window filter over 70–150 Hz and downsampled to 100 Hz.
entries.unit: Hz band; filter order; Hz feature sampling rate
entries.condition: Hilbert-transform envelope of the filtered ECoG signal.

entries.text: The article reports z-scored high-gamma time courses relative to a 500 ms pre-auditory-stimulus baseline.
entries.condition: Figure 2 caption specifies the baseline; the exact normalization procedure for classifier inputs is not further detailed.

entries.text: Listening and overt epochs ran from 100 ms before speech onset to 100 ms after offset; imagined epochs were fixed 1.5 s from visual-cue onset.
entries.unit: ms relative to onset/offset; ms imagined epoch
entries.condition: Imagined-speech onset and offset were not behaviorally observed; epochs therefore used cue onset.
entries.quote: For the imagined speech condition, because there was no speech output we extracted fixed 1.5 s epochs starting at cue onset.

entries.text: Mean listening-stimulus duration was 800 ± 20 ms; mean overt word duration was 766 ± 84 ms.
entries.condition: Across words; listening and overt speech respectively.

entries.text: The imagined-hearing cue followed the auditory word after 800 ms and lasted 1,500 ms; after a 500 ms blank, the overt-repetition cue lasted another 1,500 ms.
entries.unit: ms cue delay; ms imagery cue; ms blank; ms overt cue
entries.condition: Participants were instructed to imagine hearing the word, rather than imagine saying or seeing it; separate classifiers were built for each condition.
entries.quote: Finally, after 500 ms of blank screen, a second cross was displayed for 1500 ms, and subjects had to repeat the word out loud.

entries.text: Imagery trials with audible speech contamination and overt trials with grammatical errors were removed; microphone and eye-tracker checks supported task monitoring.
entries.condition: The auditory cue supplied the intended word label; the microphone checked for audible speech during imagery and monitored overt behavior.
entries.loc: Materials and Methods > Subjects and data acquisition; Experimental paradigm

entries.text: Per-electrode DTW distances formed kernel matrices that were combined by a discriminative-power-weighted average for the SVM.
entries.condition: Discriminative power was the ROC area based on within-class versus between-class distances.
entries.loc: Results > Classification; Materials and Methods > SVM-Kernel computation; Discriminative power index computation

entries.text: Outer evaluation used leave-one-out cross-validation, with one sample per class held out in each fold; accuracy was averaged over outer-fold test predictions.
entries.unit: test sample per class per fold
entries.condition: Trial-level, within-study cross-validation; no independent external test set is described.
entries.quote: the test set was composed of one sample per class for each fold.
entries.loc: Materials and Methods > Classifier training and performance evaluation

entries.text: An inner leave-one-out loop and grid search selected free parameters; the discriminative power index was computed on training data.
entries.condition: Inner-loop choices were fixed before outer-fold testing; no separate validation cohort is reported.
entries.loc: Materials and Methods > Classifier training and performance evaluation

entries.text: Pairwise significance used 1,000 label-shuffle randomization tests per condition and FDR correction.
entries.condition: Each shuffle repeated the feature extraction, split, DTW, kernel, inner grid search, model fitting, and outer test evaluation.
entries.quote: we randomly shuffled 1,000 times the trial labels, and applied the exact same approach as in the actual classification process

entries.text: The authors set chance accuracy for two-class classification at 50%.
entries.condition: Binary classification between a pair of words; tests compare observed accuracy with chance.

entries.text: No random-number seed is reported for the 1,000 permutation shuffles, and no separate repeated-run analysis is described.
entries.condition: The paper specifies 1,000 label shuffles but not seed, RNG, or repeated independent CV runs.

entries.text: No independent external test cohort or held-out session evaluation is reported; performance is estimated with within-study cross-validation.
entries.condition: The test fold contains one trial per class; the article does not describe a separate test set or session-wise partition.

questions.q: DTW versus no alignment: numbers, test and comparison unit
questions.answer: For overt and imagined speech, average accuracy was reduced without DTW alignment (p < 0.05; two-sample t-test; FDR correction). The comparison unit is not stated: the text does not say whether it was across subjects, word pairs, or both; it only says average classification accuracy.

questions.q: First-demonstration claim context; citations of scalp EEG/MEG imagined-speech classification and of Leuthardt 2011
questions.answer: The sentence before the claim is: “This provides preliminary evidence that superior temporal gyrus alone could drive auditory imagery decoding, but that other areas such as frontal cortex and sensorimotor cortex could also contribute.” The claim is: “Our results provide the first demonstration of single-trial neural decoding of words during imagined speech production.” No scalp EEG/MEG study of imagined/unspoken-speech classification is cited; the Wang occurrence is a coauthor name in the Wodlinger electrode-characteristics reference, not such a study. The text does not list a Leuthardt-first-author 2011 J. Neural Eng. ECoG speech-network BCI paper. It does list Pei et al. (2011), J. Neural Eng., “Decoding vowels and consonants in spoken and imagined words using electrocorticographic signals in humans,” with E. C. Leuthardt as a coauthor.

questions.q: Usable trials per class and electrodes per subject
questions.answer: not stated for either usable post-rejection trials per class per subject or electrodes per subject; the text gives 18–24 randomly repeated trials per word, not post-rejection usable counts or electrode counts.

questions.q: Word length / duration confound and identity of significant imagined pairs
questions.answer: No analysis relating pair accuracy to word length, syllable count, or acoustic-duration differences is reported. The identities of the significant imagined-speech pairs are not stated (the text reports only 8 of 15 significant). The stimulus set was designed to vary acoustic features and syllable count while minimizing word-length variance.

questions.q: Are weighting and parameter selection inside training folds
questions.answer: Yes. Optimal free parameters were selected by inner leave-one-out cross-validation using the outer training data and fixed for test evaluation; the discriminative power index was computed on the training set.

questions.q: Subvocalization controls beyond microphone and eye tracker
questions.answer: No EMG recording or explicit subvocalization-control method is reported beyond the microphone and eye tracker; the paper also screened imagined ECoG trials to remove those contaminated by overt speech.

questions.q: Suppes 1997: recording, internal-speech condition, method, best and single-trial results
questions.answer: The best internal-speech result was 91% for S1 in the O/E condition, using 7 words; chance was 1/7 (about 14.3%). Each test sample averaged 10 trials (five test samples per word, 35 total); O/E prototypes averaged 50 odd trials per word. Single-trial: 46, 39, 43% in three 105-trial blocks (S1, 7 words).
